{{recipe}}| [[Cookbook:Pasta|Pasta]] | [[Cookbook:Cuisine of Italy|Italian cuisine]]

==Ingredients==
*300 [[Cookbook:Gram|g]] (1½ [[Cookbook:Cup|cups]]) [[Cookbook:All-purpose flour|all-purpose flour]] or durum [[Cookbook:Semolina|semolina]] flour
*1 [[Cookbook:Teaspoon|tsp]] [[Cookbook:Salt|salt]]

*3 [[Cookbook:Egg|eggs]]
*1 [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|Tbsp]] [[Cookbook:Olive Oil|olive oil]]
* A few drops of water

==Procedure==

=== Dough ===
#Pour the flour and salt into a [[Cookbook:Food Processor|food processor]].
#[[Cookbook:Beating|Beat]] the eggs with the oil. With the processor running, slowly pour the egg through the feed tube.
#Continue to mix until the [[Cookbook:Dough|dough]] comes together and forms a ball. If it doesn't form a ball, add a little water through the feed tube 1 teaspoon at a time until it does.
#Remove the dough from the food processor and [[Cookbook:Kneading|knead]] for 10 minutes on a floured work surface. If the dough is too sticky, work in a little extra flour.
#Wrap the dough in some [[Cookbook:Plastic Wrap|cling wrap]] and let it rest in the refrigerator for 30 minutes.
#Remove from the fridge and knead it some more until it has warmed to room temperature.

=== Shaping ===

==== By hand ====

# Divide the dough into 2 balls.
# [[Cookbook:Dough#Rolling|Roll]] each ball out on a floured surface or pastry cloth in the shape of a rectangle.
# Rotate the dough 90º and roll across its width.
# Rotate 90º and roll some more. Keep turning and rolling until the dough is paper thin.
# If at any time the dough begins to stick, lift it carefully and flour the work surface.
# Dust the rectangle of rolled dough lightly and let it rest for 10 minutes.
#Roll it up from the shorter side into a roulade (jelly-roll) shape.
#With a sharp knife, slice the roll into even strips as follows:
#*3 [[Cookbook:Mm|mm]] (⅛ [[Cookbook:Inch|inch]]) wide (''tagliarini)''
#* 6 mm (¼ inch) wide (''fetuccine'' and ''tagliatelle'')
#* 100 mm (4 inches) wide (''lasagna)''

==== By pasta machine ====
#Cut the dough into roughly 3 equal pieces.
#On its widest setting, feed each piece of dough through the [[Cookbook:Pasta Maker|machine]] 5 or 6 times, folding it in thirds between each rolling, until smooth, shiny and elastic.
#Set the machine to the second setting and feed a portion of the dough through.
#Set the machine to the third setting and roll the dough through again.
#Keep changing the setting and rolling until the dough is about 1 mm (1/16 inch) thick.
#Use the appropriate attachment to cut the pasta into strips.

=== '''Storing''' ===
#Hang the pasta over a clean broomstick handle to dry, supported on the backs of two chairs. Or place on waxed paper or clean tea towels.
# Homemade pasta may be cooked immediately or wrapped, well floured, in cling wrap and refrigerated for up to 24 hours.
#Cook fresh pasta in 6–8 [[Cookbook:Liter|litres]] of water for 5–10 minutes or until [[Cookbook:Al dente|''al dente'']].
